title: Client limit file (Finspot OMS)
purpose: Trading limit values per client before the market opens (BOD), and the limit changes of pay-out holds during the day. Finspot's RMS limit upload has 54 columns, all listed here. Finspot computes the limit itself, so Ledgerline writes, per client across exchanges, segments and products: the account ID (1), the client's ledger balance as is (5: end of the previous business day, negative when the client owes, less cheques not yet cleared), the group wise validation indicator (17, no by default) and the notional cash (25: pledged cash-equivalent collateral after haircut: government securities, T-bills, SDLs, and the liquid fund / ETF ISINs the firm lists), and the line ends after column 25 (trailing_empty: a line may stop before the columns Ledgerline does not fill, typed blank here, or columns 17 and 25, marked may_omit, so SharePro's 5-field lines read with no issues too). Non-cash pledged securities are not in this line: they go in the ISIN Holding file as collateral with their haircut, and Finspot adds them. A client who may not take new positions (blocked, inactive, no segment open) gets the lower of the balance and 0 and no notional cash. A pay-out hold line is the same line with the amount held taken off column 5; a release line puts it back. Finspot carries the equity segments only: column 5 is meant to be the equity balance, and is the whole client ledger until segment-wise client ledgers exist. The account ID is the UCC with the firm's account ID suffix (Connections → Finspot uploads), 10 characters at most: the file is refused for longer ones.
